content.text: Now let me also spot-check that the `executor` property spread in `opts.executor.run(...)` is type-safe. The `CommandExecutorInput` has `runId, command, args, cwd, env, timeoutSec, graceSec, onLog` — and `opts` has exactly those fields (plus optional `executor`). The spread `{ runId, command, args, ...opts }` will include `executor` in the spread, but `CommandExecutorInput` doesn't have that field. TypeScript in strict mode may flag the extra property if `run` is typed as taking exactly `CommandExecutorInput`. Let me fix the call to be explicit:
